provenance.citation: McAllester, D., & Rosenblitt, D. (1991). Systematic Nonlinear Planning. In: Proceedings of the Ninth National Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-91), pp. 634–639.
provenance.locus: The Sussman anomaly (three-block problem, initial: C on A, A and B on table; goals: A on B and B on C), the canonical example motivating nonlinear/partial-order planning that SNLP solves systematically; threat resolution by promotion/demotion per the paper's causal-link semantics.
provenance.notes: Blocks-world operators are propositionalized (no variables, per the breed's propositional STRIPS contract): put_c_from_a_on_table, put_a_on_b, put_b_on_c with the standard pre/add/del lists. The only valid solution order is the interleaved c-to-table, b-on-c, a-on-b — unreachable by linear goal-at-a-time planning, which is the anomaly the paper addresses. The plan requires causal-link threat detection (put_a_on_b deletes clear_b needed by put_b_on_c; put_b_on_c deletes clear_c needed by put_c_from_a_on_table) and resolution by ordering.

input.intent: solve the Sussman anomaly with SNLP causal-link planning

expected.notes: The interleaved solution order; threat detection and promotion/demotion steps must appear in the trace.
